And the clause: «ربّي الله ... » in the position of the accusative; maqūl al-qawl.
And the clause: «جاءكم ... » in the position of the accusative; ḥāl from (رجلا), or from the agent of يقول.
And the clause: «إن يك كاذبا ... » in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause أتقتلون ...
And the clause: «عليه كذبه ... » in the position of the jussive; apodosis of the condition accompanied by the fāʾ.
And the clause: «إن يك صادقا..» in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause إن يك كاذبا.
And the clause: «يصبكم بعض ... » has no grammatical position; apodosis of the condition, not accompanied by the fāʾ.
And the clause: «يعدكم ... » has no grammatical position; ṣila of the relative (الذي).
And the clause: «إنّ الله لا يهدي..» has no grammatical position; a resumption within the scope of the saying.
And the clause: «لا يهدي ... » in the position of the nominative; khabar of إنّ.
And the clause: «هو مسرف ... » has no grammatical position; ṣila of the relative (من).
(29) (قوم) the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the implied fatḥa on the letter before the (yāʾ) omitted for lightness, and it (the yāʾ) is muḍāf ilayhi. (لكم) attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ الملك. (اليوم) adverb of time, accusative, attached to the "being established" to which the khabar is attached. (ظاهرين) ḥāl, accusative, from the pronoun in (لكم). (في الأرض) attached to ظاهرين. (الفاء) connecting the apodosis of an implied condition. (من) interrogative noun in the position of the nominative; mubtadaʾ. (من بأس) attached to (ينصرنا), by its being given the sense of "rescues us". (جاءنا) indeclinable past verb in the position of the jussive; protasis. (ما) negation. (إلّا) for restriction. (ما) relative noun in the position of the accusative; second direct object, its governing verb being أريكم, i.e. "I inform you". (الواو) conjunction. (سبيل) second direct object.
And the vocative clause: «يا قوم» has no grammatical position; a resumption within the scope of the saying.
And the clause: «لكم الملك ... » has no grammatical position; the response to the vocative.
And the clause: «من ينصرنا ... » in the position of the jussive; apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if the punishment of Allah comes, who will help us against it?"
And the clause: «ينصرنا ... » in the position of the nominative; khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
And the clause: «إن جاءنا ... » has no grammatical position; an explanation of the implied condition.
And the clause: «قال فرعون....» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «ما أريكم ... » in the position of the accusative; maqūl al-qawl.
And the clause: «أرى ... » has no grammatical position; ṣila of the relative (ما).
And the clause: «ما أهديكم ... » in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause ما أريكم.
(30) (الواو) conjunction. (عليكم) attached to (أخاف). (مثل) direct object, accusative..
And the clause: «قال الذي آمن ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause قال فرعون.
And the clause: «آمن ... » has no grammatical position; ṣila of the relative (الذي).
And the clause: «يا قوم (the second)» has no grammatical position; parenthetical, for the sake of warning.
And the clause: «إنّي أخاف ... » in the position of the accusative; maqūl al-qawl.
And the clause: «أخاف عليكم ... » in the position of the nominative; khabar of إنّ.
(31) (مثل) the second, a badal for the first, accusative. (من بعدهم) attached to an omitted element, the ṣila of the relative الذين. (الواو) parenthetical. (ما) negation operating as ليس. (للعباد) attached to (ظلما).
And the clause: «ما الله يريد ... » has no grammatical position; parenthetical.
And the clause: «يريد ظلما ... » in the position of the accusative; khabar of ما.
(32-33) (الواو) conjunction. (يا قوم.. يوم التناد) like يا قوم.. يوم الأحزاب,
in words and clauses; and the sign of the genitive in (التناد) is the implied kasra on the yāʾ omitted to suit the verse ending (fāṣila). (يوم) badal for the first يوم, accusative like it. (مدبرين) corroborating ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida) from the agent of تولّون. (ما) negation, inoperative. (لكم) attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ عاصم. (من الله) attached to عاصم. (عاصم) genitive in form and nominative in position; mubtadaʾ. (الواو) conjunction. (من) conditional noun that jazms, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative as a fronted direct object, and (يضلل) is vowelled with kasra because two sākin letters meet. (الفاء) connecting the apodosis. (ما له من هاد) like ما لكم من عاصم, and the sign of the genitive in (هاد) is the implied kasra on the omitted (yāʾ), so it is a defective noun.
And the clause: «تولّون ... » in the position of the genitive; muḍāf ilayhi..
And the clause: «ما لكم من الله من عاصم» in the position of the accusative; ḥāl from the agent of تولّون.
And the clause: «يضلل الله ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause that is the response to the vocative «[Note: and that is the clause إنّي أخاف عليكم يوم التناد.]».
And the clause: «ما له من هاد» in the position of the jussive; apodosis of the condition accompanied by the fāʾ.

* Morphology:
(29) الرشاد: a samāʿī maṣdar of the triliteral رشد of the bāb of نصر; its wazn is فعال with fatḥa on the fāʾ, and there is another maṣdar of the verb, رشد, with ḍamma then sukūn.
(32) التناد: its origin is التنادي, maṣdar of the quinary تنادى; the letter before the last should by rule have ḍamma, but it took kasra to suit the (yāʾ).. It contains an ʿilāl by substitution first, because the alif in it originates from a (wāw), from al-nadwa, which is the meeting place where those present call to one another; and an ʿilāl by deletion second, to suit the verse endings; its wazn is التفاع.

* Rhetoric:
Al-kalām al-munṣif (the fair-minded speech): in His saying, the Exalted: «أَتَقْتُلُونَ رَجُلًا أَنْ يَقُولَ رَبِّيَ اللَّهُ».
This believing man drew them on gradually by citing in witness to the truthfulness of Moses, peace be upon him, that he had come from the One to whom lordship is ascribed, with several clear proofs and not a single one, and he brought them as definite, to soften their obstinacy and break their vehemence. Then he took them in argument by way of division (taqsīm), saying: he must be either truthful or lying; if he is lying, the harm of his lie falls back upon him; or if he is truthful, you are targeted to be afflicted with some of what he promises you. He mentioned only "some" even on the assumption that he is a truthful prophet, and a prophet is truthful in all he promises, because he took with them the path of sincere advice and gentle handling.

safi-cedvel:69-76.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is for an interrogation of astonishment. (إلى الذين) is attached to (تر) in the sense of تنظر (look). (في ايات) is attached to (يجادلون). (أنّي) is an interrogative noun in the sense of كيف (how), in the position of accusative, a ḥāl, its governor being يصرفون, and the (الواو) in (يصرفون) is the deputy agent.
The clause «لم تر ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause «يجادلون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
And the clause «يصرفون ... » is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from the relative (الذين) [Note: or it has no position, an explanatory resumption.].
(70) (الذين) is a badal (substitute) for the first relative, in the position of genitive [Note: or it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause سوف يعلمون, with the fāʾ added.]. (بالكتاب) is attached to (كذّبوا), and likewise (بما), which is conjoined to it. (به) is attached to a ḥāl from رسلنا. (الفاء) is the connective of an implied condition. (سوف) is a particle of futurity.
And the clause «كذّبوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
And the clause «أرسلنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (ما).
And the clause «يعلمون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "when the punishment comes, they will know".
(71) - (إذ) is an adverb borrowed for the future, in the position of accusative, attached to (يعلمون) [Note: or it is a direct object of the verb يعلمون, i.e. "they will know the time when the shackles are on their necks".]. (في أعناقهم) is attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ الأغلال. (السلاسل) is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause يسحبون, the linking pronoun being implied, i.e. "by them" [Note: it is permissible that it be conjoined to الأغلال, the conjunction then being a conjunction of single words.].
And the clause «الأغلال في أعناقهم..» is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause «السلاسل يسحبون (بها)» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause الأغلال.
And the clause «يسحبون (بها)» is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ السلاسل.
(72) (في الحميم) is attached to (يسحبون). (في النار) is attached to (يسجرون), and the (الواو) in the two verbs is the deputy agent.
And the clause «يسجرون..» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause الأغلال ... [Note: or to the clause السلاسل يسحبون.].
(73) - (لهم) is attached to (قيل). (أين) is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative, an adverb of place, attached to an omitted fronted khabar for the mubtadaʾ (ما), which is a relative noun, the returning pronoun being omitted.
And the clause «قيل ... » is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause يسجرون.
And the clause «أين ما كنتم ... » is in the position of nominative, the deputy agent.
And the clause «كنتم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (ما).
And the clause «تشركون» is in the position of accusative, the khabar of كنتم.
(74) - (من دون) is attached to a ḥāl from the omitted returning pronoun. (عنّا) is attached to (ضلّوا), by making it include the meaning of "they were absent". (بل) is for transitional disregard (iḍrāb intiqālī). (قبل) is an adverbial noun indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of genitive, attached to (ندعو). (شيئا) is a direct object, accusative [Note: it is permissible that it be an absolute object standing in for the maṣdar, i.e. "we were not worshipping anything of worship when we worshipped them".]. (كذلك) is attached to an omitted absolute object, its governor being يضلّ.
And the clause «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption.
And the clause «ضلّوا ... » is in the position of accusative, the content of the saying.
And the clause «لم نكن ندعو ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause «ندعو ... » is in the position of accusative, the khabar of نكن.
And the clause «يضل الله ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
(75) - (بما) is attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ «ذلكم», the indication in it being to the punishment. (في الأرض) is attached to (تفرحون). (بغير) is a ḥāl from the agent of تفرحون. (الواو) is a conjunction. (بما كنتم تمرحون) is like بما كنتم تفرحون.
And the clause «ذلكم بما كنتم ... » is in the position of accusative, the content of an implied saying.
And the clause «كنتم تفرحون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (ما).
And the clause «تفرحون..» is in the position of accusative, the khabar of كنتم.
And the clause «كنتم تمرحون..» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative (ما).
And the clause «تمرحون..» is in the position of accusative, the khabar of كنتم.
(76) - (خالدين) is an accusative ḥāl from the agent of ادخلوا. (فيها) is attached to خالدين. (الفاء) is resumptive [Note: or the connective of an implied condition.], and the specified of the censure (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being "هي", i.e. Jahannam.
And the clause «ادخلوا ... » has no grammatical position; a resumption within the sphere of the implied saying.
And the clause «بئس مثوى المتكبّرين» has no grammatical position; resumptive [Note: or the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you enter Jahannam, then wretched is the abode of the disbelievers — it, that is, then wretched is the entrance.."].

* Morphology:
(71) - السلاسل: plural of السلسلة, a well-known noun; its wazn is فعللة, with kasra on the fāʾ and the first lām; and the wazn of سلاسل is فعالل.

* Benefits:
- The apodosis and the quasi-apodosis:
Just as the fāʾ links the apodosis to its condition, so it links the quasi-apodosis to the quasi-condition, as in our saying (الذي يأتيني فله درهم) ("Whoever comes to me, he has a dirham"). By its entry is understood what the speaker intended of the dependence of the obligation of the dirham upon the coming; and had it not entered, that and other things would be possible. A similar example occurs in the verse we are dealing with, in the words of the Exalted الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِالْكِتابِ وَبِما أَرْسَلْنا بِهِ رُسُلَنا فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ: the relative noun in the noble verse carries the meaning of a condition, so the fāʾ came to link the quasi-apodosis with the quasi-condition, because the relative noun is not a pure condition. And this fāʾ is in the position of the preparatory lām (lām al-tawṭiʾa) in the words of the Exalted لَئِنْ أُخْرِجُوا لا يَخْرُجُونَ مَعَهُمْ, in that it announces what the speaker intended of the meaning of the oath. And the words of the Exalted وَما أَصابَكُمْ مِنْ مُصِيبَةٍ فَبِما كَسَبَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ have been read with it retained, i.e. it was read with the fāʾ retained and with it omitted.
Abū l-Baqāʾ al-ʿUkbarī says: Among the readers, whoever omitted the fāʾ took it as being like the words of the Exalted وَإِنْ أَطَعْتُمُوهُمْ إِنَّكُمْ لَمُشْرِكُونَ, and like what came in the saying of the poet — the verse is ascribed to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥassān:
من يفعل الحسنات الله يشكرها ... والشر بالشر عند الله مثلان
(Whoever does good deeds, Allah thanks him for them ... and evil for evil, with Allah, are two equals.)
And it is permissible on this view to make (ما) in the sense of (الذي), but there is weakness in it. And Allah knows best.

safi-cedvel:77-77.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive in the two places. (إن) is a conditional particle that jazzes. (ما) is redundant. (نرينّك) is an imperfect verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). (بعض) is a second direct object, accusative. (الذي) is a relative in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi. (أو) is a conjunction. (نتوفّينّك) is like (نرينّك), by conjunction. (الفاء) is the connective of the apodosis. (إلينا) is attached to (يرجعون), and the (الواو) in it is the deputy agent.
The clause «اصبر ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause «إنّ وعد الله حقّ» has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption.
And the clause «إمّا نرينّك ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive ... and the apodosis is omitted, i.e. "that is a clear matter".
And the clause «نعدهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
And the clause «نتوفّينّك ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause نرينّك.
And the clause «إلينا يرجعون» is in the position of nominative, the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هم", and the nominal clause is in the position of jussive, the apodosis of the second condition [Note: it is permissible that the clause be the apodosis of both conditions together, the implied form then being: "(whether We punish them in your lifetime or do not punish them, We shall punish them in the Hereafter)".].

safi-cedvel:78-78.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (اللام) is the lām of oath, for an implied oath. (قد) is a particle of confirmation. (من قبلك) is attached to (أرسلنا) [Note: or attached to an adjective of (رسلا).]. (منهم) is attached to a fronted khabar for the mubtadaʾ (من). (عليك) is attached to (قصصنا). (الواو) is a conjunction in the two places. (ما) is negative. (لرسول) is attached to an omitted element that is the khabar of كان. (بآية) is attached to (يأتي). (إلّا) is for exception. (بإذن) is attached to an omitted ḥāl, excepted from the generality of states.
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن يأتي ... ) is in the position of nominative, the ism of كان [Note: and the implied form is: "the bringing of a sign was not permitted to a messenger in any state except the state of its being by the leave of Allah".].
(الفاء) is a conjunction. (بالحقّ) is the deputy agent [Note: or attached to (قضي), and the deputy agent is omitted, being the maṣdar of the verb, i.e. the judgement.]. (هنالك) is a demonstrative in the position of accusative, an adverb of place, attached to (خسر) [Note: or borrowed for time.].
The clause «أرسلنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the oath ... and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause «منهم من قصصنا ... » has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption [Note: or in the position of accusative, a second adjective of (رسلا).].
And the clause «قصصنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (من).
And the clause «منهم من لم نقصص ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause منهم من قصصنا.
And the clause «لم نقصص ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative (من).
And the clause «ما كان لرسول ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أرسلنا.
And the clause «يأتي ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
And the clause «جاء أمر ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause «قضي بالحقّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
And the clause «خسر ... المبطلون» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause قضي بالحقّ.

safi-cedvel:79-81.t:
* I'rab:
(لكم) is attached to (جعل), by making it include the meaning of "created" [Note: or attached to an omitted second direct object, its implied form being "mounts", by the evidence of His words: لتركبوا.]. (اللام) is for cause. (تركبوا) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the lām. (منها) is attached to (تركبوا), and من is for beginning or partitive. (الواو) is resumptive. (منها) is attached to the verb تأكلون. (لكم) is a fronted khabar. (فيها) is attached to a ḥāl from منافع — or to the omitted khabar. (منافع) is a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative. (لتبلغوا) is like لتركبوا. (عليها) is attached to a ḥāl from the agent of تبلغوا..
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن تركبوا) is in the position of genitive by the (اللام), attached to (جعل).
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن تبلغوا) is in the position of genitive by the (اللام), attached to (جعل), conjoined to the first maṣdar.
(عليها، على الفلك) are both attached to (تحملون), and the (الواو) in it is the deputy agent. (في صدوركم) is an adjective of حاجة.
(آياته) is a second direct object, accusative. (الفاء) is resumptive. (أيّ) is an interrogative noun of rebuke, a fronted direct object, accusative.
The clause «الله الذي ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause «جعل..» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
And the clause «تركبوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-type relative (أن).
And the clause «تأكلون» has no grammatical position; resumptive [Note: or parenthetical.].
And the clause «لكم فيها منافع ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the last resumptive clause.
And the clause «تبلغوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second implied particle-type relative (أن).
And the clause «تحملون» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause «يريكم» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause تحملون [Note: or conjoined to the ṣila clause جعل لكم.. with what is between the two clauses being parenthetical.].
And the clause «تنكرون» has no grammatical position; resumptive.

safi-cedvel:34-34.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (اللام) the lām of oath, for an implied oath. (قد) particle of certainty. (قبل) adverbial noun, indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of the genitive, attached to (جاءكم). (بالبيّنات) attached to a ḥāl from يوسف. (الفاء) conjunction. (في شكّ) attached to the khabar of ما زلتم. (ممّا) attached to شكّ. (به) attached to a ḥāl from the agent of (جاءكم) «[Note: or attached to (جاءكم).]». (حتّى) particle of commencement. (من بعده) attached to (يبعث). (كذلك) attached to an omitted absolute (muṭlaq) element, whose governing verb is يضلّ. (من) relative noun; direct object. (مرتاب) second khabar, nominative.
Clause: «جاءكم يوسف ... » has no grammatical position; the response to the implied oath..
And the implied oath clause has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «ما زلتم ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause that is the response to the oath.
And the clause: «جاءكم به ... » has no grammatical position; ṣila of the relative (ما).
And the clause: «هلك ... » in the position of the genitive; muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «قلتم ... » has no grammatical position; apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
And the clause: «لن يبعث الله ... » in the position of the accusative; maqūl al-qawl.
And the clause: «يضل الله ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «هو مسرف ... » has no grammatical position; ṣila of the relative (من).

* Morphology:
(زلتم): it contains an ʿilāl by deletion, to suit the indeclinability on sukūn, so the ʿayn of the verb was dropped because of the two sākin letters; its wazn is فلتم.
(مرتاب): an active participle from the quinary ارتاب, whose imperfect is يرتاب; its ʿayn underwent ʿilāl because it is from al-rayb, its origin being يرتيب, with fatḥa on the tāʾ and kasra on the yāʾ, then the yāʾ was changed to alif because it is vowelled and what precedes it has fatḥa. When the active participle was formed from it, the ʿilāl remained as it was; its wazn is مفتعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.. It is also permissible that the word (مرتاب) be a passive participle too, in another expression.

safi-cedvel:35-35.t:
* I'rab:
(في آيات) attached to (يجادلون). (بغير) attached to a ḥāl from the agent of يجادلون. The agent of (كبر) is a pronoun referring to the maṣdar of يجادلون understood from the context, i.e. "their disputing was great in hatefulness" «[Note: it is permissible that the agent be omitted, indicated by the context, i.e. "their saying was great in hatefulness".]». (مقتا) tamyīz transposed from the agent, accusative. (عند) adverb, accusative, attached to (مقتا), and likewise the second (عند), which is conjoined to it. (كذلك) attached to an omitted absolute (muṭlaq) element, whose governing verb is يطبع. (على كلّ) attached to (يطبع). (جبّار) adjective of (متكبّر), genitive like it.
Clause: «الذين يجادلون ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive «[Note: or it is a resumption within the scope of the speech of the believer mentioned earlier.]».
And the clause: «يجادلون ... » has no grammatical position; ṣila of the relative (الذين).
And the clause: «كبر (جدالهم) ... » in the position of the nominative; khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين) «[Note: It is permissible that the khabar be omitted, its implied form being "obstinate ones", the clause being resumptive.. and some of them]».
[Translator's note: the final note in the source breaks off with "and some of them".]
And the clause: «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; ṣila of the second relative (الذين).
And the clause: «يطبع ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.

* Benefits:
- A glance at «كلّ»:
It is a noun coined for the comprehension of the individuals of an indefinite, as in His saying, the Exalted: «كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ»; of a definite plural, as in «وَكُلُّهُمْ آتِيهِ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ فَرْداً»; and of the parts of a definite singular, as in "كل زيد حسن". So if you say "أكلت كلّ رغيف لزيد" it is for the generality of individuals; but if you annex "loaf" to Zayd, it becomes for the generality of the parts of a single individual. From this it is necessary, in the reading of other than Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Dhakwān in the verse we are dealing with, «كَذلِكَ يَطْبَعُ اللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ قَلْبِ مُتَكَبِّرٍ جَبَّارٍ», without tanwīn on قلب, to imply (كل) after (قلب), so that it covers the individual hearts as it covers the parts of the heart.
And (كل) occurs, with regard to each of what precedes and follows it, in three ways:
1- It may be an adjective of an indefinite or a definite, indicating its perfection, and it must be annexed to an overt noun identical to it in word and meaning, as in "أطعمنا شاة كلّ شاة" and the saying of al-Ashhab ibn Rumayla:
وإن الذي حانت بفلج دماؤهم ... هم القوم كلّ القوم يا أمّ خالد
(Truly those whose blood was shed at Falj, they are the people, the whole of the people, O Umm Khālid.)
2- It may be emphasis (tawkīd) of a definite, and it must be annexed to a pronoun referring to the emphasised word, as in His saying, the Exalted: «فَسَجَدَ الْمَلائِكَةُ كُلُّهُمْ أَجْمَعُونَ».
3- It may be following, rather coming after the governors, occurring annexed to an overt noun, as in «كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِما كَسَبَتْ رَهِينَةٌ», and not annexed, as in «وَكُلًّا ضَرَبْنا لَهُ الْأَمْثالَ». And know that the word كل takes the ruling of singular and indefinite, and its meaning is according to what it is annexed to.

safi-cedvel:36-37.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (لي) attached to (ابن). (أسباب) badal for the first الأسباب, accusative. (الفاء) the fāʾ of causation. (أطلع) imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the (الفاء). (إلى إله) attached to (أطلع) ..
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن أطّلع ... ) is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to a maṣdar extracted from the preceding command, i.e. "let there be building from you, then looking out from me".
(37) (الواو) conjunction. (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis. (الواو) resumptive. (كذلك) attached to an omitted absolute (muṭlaq) element, whose governing verb is زيّن. (لفرعون) attached to (زيّن). (عن السبيل) attached to (صدّ). (الواو) conjunction. (ما) negation, inoperative. (إلّا) for restriction. (في تباب) khabar of the mubtadaʾ كيد ...
Clause: «قال فرعون ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the vocative clause and its response.. in the position of the accusative; maqūl al-qawl.
And the clause: «ابن ... » has no grammatical position; the response to the vocative.
And the clause: «لعلّي أبلغ ... » has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «أبلغ الأسباب ... » in the position of the nominative; khabar of لعلّ.
And the clause: «أطّلع ... » has no grammatical position; ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).
And the clause: «إنّي لأظنّه ... » in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause that is the maqūl al-qawl.
And the clause: «أظنّه كاذبا ... » in the position of the nominative; khabar of إنّ.
And the clause: «زيّن ... سوء عمله» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «صدّ ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause زيّن.
And the clause: «ما كيد فرعون إلّا ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause زيّن «[Note: or it is another resumptive clause.]».

* Morphology:
(تباب): a samāʿī maṣdar of the verb تبّ of the bāb of نصر; its wazn is فعال with fatḥa on the fāʾ. The verb has other maṣdars: تبّ on the wazn فعل with fatḥa then sukūn, تبب with two fatḥas, and تبيب on the wazn فعيل; all of them mean destruction and loss.

safi-cedvel:82-85.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is for interrogation in the sense of intimidation and rebuke. (الفاء) is a conjunction in the three places. (في الأرض) is attached to (يسيروا). (ينظروا) is an imperfect verb in the jussive, conjoined to (يسيروا) [Note: it is permissible that it be accusative by an implied أن after the fāʾ, with (الفاء) causal (sababiyya), an interrogative having preceded it.
And see verse (21) of this sūra, for this is the like of that.]. (كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative, the khabar of كان. (من قبلهم) is attached to an omitted element that is the ṣila of the relative الذين. (منهم) is attached to أكثر. (قوّة) is a tamyīz (specification) of أشدّ, accusative. (في الأرض) is attached to an adjective of آثار. (ما) is negative [Note: or interrogative, in the position of accusative, a direct object of the verb أغنى.], and the second is a maṣdar particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of nominative, the returning pronoun being omitted.]. (عنهم) is attached to (أغنى).
The clause «لم يسيروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. "were they unable, so that they did not travel".
And the clause «ينظروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يسيروا [Note: it is permissible that it be the ṣila of the implied particle-type relative (أن), if the fāʾ is causal after an interrogative.].
And the clause «كان عاقبة ... » is in the position of accusative, a direct object of the verb of looking, which is suspended by the interrogative, on the assumption of the preposition..
And the clause «كانوا ... » has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption.
And the clause «ما أغنى ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause كانوا ...
And the clause «كانوا ... (the second)» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (ما).
And the interpreted maṣdar (ما كانوا يكسبون) is in the position of nominative, the agent of أغنى.
And the clause «يكسبون ... » is in the position of accusative, the khabar of كانوا.
(83) (الفاء) is a conjunction. (لمّا) is an adverb in the sense of "when", including the meaning of a condition, in the position of accusative, attached to the apodosis فرحوا. (بالبيّنات) is attached to a ḥāl from رسلهم. (بما) is attached to (فرحوا). (عندهم) is an adverb, accusative, attached to an omitted element that is the ṣila of the relative ما. (من العلم) is a ḥāl from the returning pronoun in the implied ṣila. (بهم) is attached to (حاق). (به) is attached to (يستهزئون).
And the clause «جاءتهم رسلهم ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi..
And the clause «فرحوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
And the clause «حاق بهم ما كانوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the apodosis.
And the clause «كانوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (ما).
And the clause «يستهزئون..» is in the position of accusative, the khabar of كانوا.
(84) (فلمّا) is like the first. (رأوا) is a past verb indeclinable on an implied ḍamma on the omitted alif, omitted because of the meeting of two sukūns.. and the (الواو) is the agent. (بالله) is attached to (آمنّا). (وحده) is an accusative ḥāl. (بما) is attached to (كفرنا). (به) is attached to مشركين.
And the clause «رأوا ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
And the clause «آمنّا ... » is in the position of accusative, the content of the saying.
And the clause «كفرنا ... » is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause آمنا..
And the clause «كنّا..» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (ما).
(85) (الفاء) is a conjunction. (يك) is a defective imperfect verb, jussive, the sign of the jussive being the sukūn on the nūn, which was omitted for lightness; and the ism of (يك) is a pronoun obligatorily latent, its implied form being "هو" (he), referring to (إيمانهم) [Note: or it is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn).] according to the rule of tanāzuʿ (dispute over governance), so the agent of (ينفعهم) is إيمانهم. (لمّا) is like the first, and is attached to the content of the apodosis. (سنّة) is an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq) of an omitted verb [Note: or a direct object of an omitted verb in the manner of warning (taḥdhīr), i.e.: "beware the way of Allah".]. (التي) is a relative noun in the position of accusative, an adjective of سنّة. (في عباده) is attached to (خلت). (الواو) is a conjunction. (خسر هنالك الكافرون): the i'rab of its like has been given [Note: in verse (78) of this sūra.].
And the clause «لم يك ينفعهم إيمانهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause قالوا [Note: or conjoined to an implied element arising from their saying آمنّا.. i.e. "so they believed, but their belief did not benefit them".].
And the clause «ينفعهم إيمانهم ... » is in the position of accusative, the khabar of يك.
And the clause «رأوا ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi ... and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e.: "when they saw Our might, their belief did not benefit them when they believed....".
And the clause « (سنّ الله) ذلك سنّة ... » has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption — or parenthetical — and the clause «قد خلت ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (التي).
And the clause «خسر هنالك الكافرون» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause لم يك ...

* Morphology:
(سنّت): the tāʾ is written extended (mabsūṭa) in the muṣḥaf, though its due is to be tied (marbūṭa).

* Rhetoric:
The art of mockery (fann al-tahakkum): in the words of the Exalted «فَرِحُوا بِما عِنْدَهُمْ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ».
They showed joy in that, namely what they had of false beliefs and refuted doubts. And calling them "knowledge" is in mockery of them.

* Benefits:
- Kinds of tanwīn:
1- Tanwīn al-tamkīn (of firm establishment): this is the one attached to a declinable noun that takes full case-endings, informing that it remains on its original state and that it does not resemble a particle so as to be indeclinable, nor a verb so as to be barred from full declension; it is also called "tanwīn al-ṣarf", as in «زيد ورجل ورجال» and the words of the Exalted in the verse we are dealing with كانُوا أَكْثَرَ مِنْهُمْ وَأَشَدَّ قُوَّةً وَآثاراً فِي الْأَرْضِ. 2- Tanwīn al-tankīr (of indefiniteness): this is the one attached to some indeclinable nouns to distinguish their definite from their indefinite; it occurs in the chapter of the nouns of verbs by transmission, as in (صه ومه وإيه), and in a proper name ending in (ويه) by analogy, as in: (جاءني سيبويه وسيبويه آخر) ("Sībawayh came to me, and another Sībawayh"). The difference between (إيه) and (إيهٍ) is that the first, without tanwīn, means "go on with your familiar talk that you are telling me", and the meaning of (إيهٍ) with tanwīn is "go on with whatever talk you wish".
As for the tanwīn of «رجل» and the like among declinable nouns, it is tanwīn al-tamkīn, not tanwīn al-tankīr, as some students may imagine; for that reason, if you named a man with it, that very tanwīn would remain while the indefiniteness had gone.
3- Tanwīn al-muqābala (of correspondence): this is the one attached to the like of (مسلمات), made to correspond to the nūn in «مسلمين». It was said: it is a compensation for the fatḥa in the accusative, but were that so it would not be given tanwīn in the nominative and genitive; and it was said: it is tanwīn al-tamkīn, which is refuted by its persisting when it is used as a name, like عرفات, just as the nūn of مسلمين persists when it is used as a name, whereas tanwīn al-tamkīn does not coexist with the two causes (of diptotism); for that reason, if one named with (مسلمة or عرفة), their tanwīn would disappear.
4- Tanwīn al-ʿiwaḍ (of compensation): this is the one attached as a compensation for an original letter, such as (جواز وغواش), for it is a compensation for the omitted yāʾ; or as a compensation for an additional letter, as in جندل, whose tanwīn is a compensation for the alif of جنادل — Ibn Mālik said this, but what appears is the opposite, that it is tanwīn al-ṣarf, and that the loss of the alif is not like the loss of the yāʾ in (جوار وغواش).
Or as a compensation for the muḍāf ilayhi, whether a single word or a clause. The single word is the tanwīn attached to (بعض وكل) when they are cut off from annexation, as in the words of the Exalted وَكُلًّا ضَرَبْنا لَهُ الْأَمْثالَ and فَضَّلْنا بَعْضَهُمْ عَلى بَعْضٍ. It was said that it is tanwīn al-tamkīn, which returned with the disappearance of the annexation that was opposing it.
As for the tanwīn of the clause, it is the one attached to (إذ), as in the words of the Exalted وَانْشَقَّتِ السَّماءُ فَهِيَ يَوْمَئِذٍ واهِيَةٌ, the implied form being (فهي يوم إذ انشقت); then the clause that was the muḍāf ilayhi was omitted because it was known, and the tanwīn was brought as a compensation for it.
5- Tanwīn al-tarannum (of chanting): this is the one attached to unrestricted rhymes (al-qawāfī al-muṭlaqa), in place of the letter of release, which is the alif, wāw and yāʾ, and that is in the recitation of Banū Tamīm; and this tanwīn is not particular to nouns, by the evidence of the saying of Jarīr:
أقلي اللوم عاذل والعتابا ... وقولي إن أصبت فقد أصابن
(Lessen the blame, O reproacher, and the reproach ... and say, "if you are right, then he has hit the mark".)
The original: أصابا; the alif is the letter of release and was replaced by a nūn for chanting.
6- Tanwīn al-ḍarūra (of necessity): this is the one attached to what is not declined (diptotes), like the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
ويوم دخلت الخدر خدر عنيزة ... فقال لك الولايات إنك مرجلي
(And the day I entered the howdah, the howdah of ʿUnayza ... and she said, "Woe to you, you will make me go on foot.") [Translator's note: the source prints "الولايات" in the second hemistich, and "عنيرة" in the following sentence; both are translated as written, and the gloss follows the commonly transmitted verse, which reads "الويلات" and "عنيزة".]
The poet gave tanwīn to «عنيرة», which is a diptote, out of necessity; and to a vocative indeclinable on the ḍamma, like the saying of al-Aḥwaṣ:
سلام الله يا مطر عليها ... وليس عليك يا مطر السلام
(The peace of Allah, O Maṭar, be upon her ... and upon you, O Maṭar, there is no peace.)
The poet gave tanwīn to «مطر», which is a vocative indeclinable on the ḍamma, to which tanwīn is not permissible except out of necessity.
